races.title: State House, District 115
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Lindsey Prather
cands.bio: North Carolina House member for District 115 (Buncombe County) since January 2023. Former special education and social studies teacher in Buncombe County Schools for six years. Holds a UNC Asheville sociology degree and a Western Carolina University MPA. Works as Assistant Director of Admissions at UNC Asheville.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina endorsed her in 2026, according to Ballotpedia.

Her 2024 Ballotpedia survey lists NCAE, Emily's List, Planned Parenthood, AFL-CIO and other labor unions, Sierra Club, and NC League of Conservation Voters as endorsers. This is her own statement and was not checked against the groups' pages.

cands.gaps: We could not find her birthplace or the year she moved to Buncombe County. We found no documented positions or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and development, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws, or school vouchers. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. Her campaign pages give general themes on education, healthcare, and the environment but no specific stances on these topics. We found no reporting on controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site says she was raised in Wake County and has lived in Buncombe County for over 16 years, and Ballotpedia lists Cary High School; her birthplace is not stated in the pages I read.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State House member since 2023 (committees included Appropriations and Local Government). Taught special education and social studies for six years, earned a Master of Public Affairs in 2019, and works in university admissions.
qual.why: She has held a legislative seat for more than three years and has a public-affairs graduate degree and a public-sector career. She has no documented law or budget career outside the legislature, so the score sits at the low end of the high range.

cands.name: Anthony J. Penland
cands.bio: Anthony Penland is chief of the Swannanoa Volunteer Fire Department in Buncombe County. He joined the department in 1990 and has been chief since 2001. He has also served there as a full-time firefighter and treasurer. He has held no elected office. He was the Republican nominee for NC House District 115 in 2026.

endorsements.text: In his Ballotpedia survey Penland lists endorsements from the NC Police Benevolent Association, the NC Fraternal Order of Police and Americans for Prosperity - North Carolina. Ballotpedia itself did not identify any endorsements for him, so these are his own claims.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Penland was born or whether he ever lived outside Buncombe County; his lifelong residence rests on his own statement. He has held no public office, so there is no legislative record to review. We found no stated positions from him on data centers, development and growth, limits on out-of-state or foreign land buyers, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site does not mention police pay or pensions, although he lists police-group endorsements. He says he will seek funding for Hurricane Helene recovery, including schools, roads and first responders, but we found no specific bills or plans. No news coverage or controversies about him turned up in the pages we had. The endorsements listed are his own claims and were not confirmed by the endorsing groups.

local.label: Roots 90: In his Ballotpedia survey Penland says he has spent his entire life in Buncombe County, graduated from Owen High School, and has served the Swannanoa fire department for 36 years. His birthplace is not independently confirmed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Fire chief of the Swannanoa Volunteer Fire Department since 2001, with earlier roles there as volunteer, full-time firefighter and treasurer. He holds an associate degree (2006) and a bachelor's in Fire and Emergency (Fayetteville State, 2015).
qual.why: He has real management experience running a public-safety organization and serving as its treasurer. He has no legislative service and no record in law or policy work, so he scores in the middle range.
